summary: Same pattern — a flat colour field with a static centre disc in a contrasting hue, both cycling hue together at an identical 6.5 s period — but the port's disc is ~12% larger in radius for the same slider value, its two zones sit 0.45 apart in hue instead of 0.40, it renders ~7% brighter, and its untouched default already draws a half-width disc where the original draws nothing.
observations: Structure (both sides, every setting tested): the 16x16 grid contains exactly TWO distinct colours — a uniform outer field and a solid, axis-centred circular disc. Confirmed by dumping whole frames: at sliderRadius=0.5 both sides give exactly 2 colours with the same 224/32 pixel split, and the disc's row/column/diagonal extents obey the 2R vs 1.41R signature of a true circle on both. Despite the name there are no multiple rings on either side at any slider value.

Motion (from *-motion.png filmstrips and *-rhythm.png, dialed sliderRadius=0.5): nothing translates. The only animation is a smooth hue rotation of the whole image; the disc never moves or changes size. Identical character on both sides — no jumps, no jitter.

Hue rate is IDENTICAL: tracking the outer field's hue across a 16 s dump, both sides advance 0.0768 hue per 0.5 s = 0.1536/s, period 6.51 s, same direction (increasing). Rate held to 3 decimal places on both sides at --fps 10, 20 and 40, so both are time-based and neither is frame-rate coupled.

HUE OFFSET: the port's outer field runs a constant +0.050 in hue ahead of the original's, at all 24 sampled times over 16 s. The inner disc's hue, by contrast, matches the original to within 0.002 at every sample. So the port's inner-to-outer hue separation is 0.451 where the original's is 0.400. Example at t=0, sliderRadius=0.5 — orig outer (0,178,79) / inner (76,3,0); port outer (0,191,142) / inner (84,3,0).

BRIGHTNESS: the port is uniformly ~7% brighter. Peak channel is 178 on the original vs 191 on the port for the outer field (consistent with value 0.70 vs 0.75), and 76 vs 84 for the disc. Constant across time, radius and grid size. 60 s survey means: orig 89.2, port 86.3 (the port's mean is lower only because its default disc is dark and large).

DISC SIZE vs SLIDER: the port's disc radius is ~12% larger than the original's for the same sliderRadius. Measured on a 48x48 re-render (to beat quantisation), disc radius as a fraction of half-grid-width is linear in the slider on both sides — orig R = 0.785 x sliderRadius, port R = 0.879 x sliderRadius. Confirmed on the DEFAULT 16x16 rig by pixel counts at t=0: slider 0.4 -> orig 16 px / port 24 px; 0.6 -> 44 / 52; 0.7 -> 52 / 68; 0.9 -> 88 / 120; 1.0 -> 112 / 148 (of 256). At slider 0.2/0.3/0.5 the 16x16 quantisation happens to hide it (4/4, 12/12, 32/32).

UNTOUCHED DEFAULTS DIVERGE: with no controls set the original renders a completely FLAT full-grid solid colour — 2304/2304 pixels one colour on a 48x48 render, i.e. default radius 0 — while the port already draws a centre disc of 432/2304 px (radius 0.49 of half-width, equivalent to sliderRadius ~0.55 on the port's own scale). A viewer loading the pattern with defaults sees a plain colour wash on the original and a two-tone bullseye on the port.

Both sides are resolution-independent in the same way: the disc scales proportionally with the grid (16x16 vs 48x48 radii agree as a fraction of half-width on each side), so the port did not introduce a native-resolution rasterisation.
Both sides are fully deterministic and seed-independent: seed 1 and seed 1234 produced byte-identical dumps on both sides.

No modes or long-period structure on either side. A 300 s / 2 fps survey shows nothing but the steady 6.5 s hue banding on both rhythm images; a --skip 150 --seconds 20 late-window check matches the early window, and brightnessTrend is 'steady' with zeroMotionFrames 1 on both. No warm-up transient, no decay, no port death.
Control surface matches exactly: both sides expose one control, sliderRadius (kind 'slider', label 'Radius'). No missing or extra dials, no kind mismatch.

dials.name: sliderRadius
dials.origEffect: Monotonically grows the centre disc from nothing (slider 0-0.1 renders flat) to a disc of radius 0.785 x half-grid-width at slider 1 (112 of 256 px on the 16x16 rig). Affects size only — hue, hue rate and brightness are untouched by it. Probe maxDelta 45.4, responsive.
dials.portEffect: Same monotonic size-only response, same direction, but ~12% larger radius at every setting: radius 0.879 x half-grid-width at slider 1 (148 of 256 px). Also renders flat only at 0-0.1. Probe maxDelta 47.0, responsive.

feedback: Disc radius is ~12% too large for a given sliderRadius. On a 48x48 grid the original's disc radius is 0.785 x (half grid width) x sliderRadius; the port's is 0.879 x that. Scale the port's radius threshold by 0.893 (equivalently, the port currently behaves like the original would at sliderRadius x 1.12). Check on the default 16x16 rig with slider=1: the original lights 112 of 256 pixels in the disc, the port lights 148.

The hue gap between the two zones is too wide. The original renders its outer field exactly 0.400 in hue above the inner disc; the port renders it 0.451 above. The inner disc's hue is already exactly right at every sampled time, so the fix belongs entirely on the outer/background hue: subtract 0.050 from it. Sanity check at sliderRadius=0.5, t=0: outer should read (0,178,79) spring-green, not (0,191,142) teal.

Overall output is ~7% too bright: the original's peak channel is 178 (value 0.70) for the outer field and 76 for the disc; the port posts 191 (value 0.75) and 84. Both zones are scaled by the same factor, so a single brightness/value constant of 0.70 instead of 0.75 fixes both.

The untouched default radius is wrong. With no control set the original draws NO disc at all — a completely flat single-colour grid (verified 2304/2304 pixels identical at 48x48) — meaning its radius global initialises to 0. The port initialises to roughly 0.55, drawing a disc of radius 0.49 x half-grid-width straight away. Initialise the port's radius state to 0 so the untouched render is a plain colour wash.

Nothing to change on timing, geometry or animation: hue period (6.51 s), hue direction, fps-invariance, disc centring and circularity, resolution scaling, seed-independence and steady-state behaviour over 300 s all already match the original exactly.
